real_arithmetic_guard_counterexample.scope: One-token state-map/active-float2-pair simulation; not a production kernel invocation or end-to-end GDN oracle.

bf16_output_cast.method: Binary32 bits: add 0x7fff + high-half LSB, shift right16; decode BF16 bits as FP32. Independently compare Torch CPU float32.to(bfloat16) bit-for-bit.
bf16_output_cast.domain: Finite normal/zero witness values only; not a proof of NaN payload, overflow, subnormal, or signed-zero special-case semantics.

limits: No CUDA calls, GPU execution, CUDA compilation, timing, graph replay, or sanitizer checks.
RN operation order follows reviewed scan_precise_chunk source; GPU implementation, dispatch selection, and full-model behavior were not validated.
BF16 q/k inputs are explicitly fixed; the Torch CPU normalization result agrees here, but CUDA normalization equivalence is not claimed.
This disproves using ideal-real contraction as a pure FP32 seed-deviation bound; it does not prove failure of an existing accepted production workload.
Values and initial state are finite but deliberately large; typical model distributions and guard false-positive/performance rates are unmeasured.
The comparator here is the same FP32 recurrence with a neighboring seed, not the independent FP64 mathematical acceptance oracle.
A sound machine-arithmetic guard needs magnitude-aware rounding reserves and all output/BF16 boundaries, plus both existing final-state error metrics.
real_arithmetic_guard_counterexample.trace_reference: Independent Fraction binary32 RN ties-to-even cross-check of separate NumPy FP32 operations and libm.fmaf
